required_work: Rebind the dormant QM tree into an executable ioi.ai surface over daemon truth: QM's Postgres state becomes daemon/Agentgres projections, its keychain UX becomes wallet-network/CapabilityLease flows, and its harness plugins become harness-registry profiles.
objective: Make the adopted QM shell executable against canonical owners only — after the orchestration seam and the participant/frontier closeout exist to be bound to. M5_QM_EXECUTABLE_REBIND_EXIT=0.
falsifiable_claim: The rebound surface reads only daemon/Agentgres projections (no Postgres truth store), crosses authority only through wallet-network/CapabilityLease, resolves harnesses only through the harness registry, and fails closed with typed unavailable states everywhere a canonical owner is absent.
selected_profile: One served ioi.ai surface over the adopted tree, bound to the verified seam and closeout owners.
in_scope: Postgres-truth-to-projection rebinding; keychain-to-CapabilityLease rebinding; plugin-to-harness-registry rebinding.
Typed unavailable/fail-closed states for absent owners.
Serving decision and route registration through the census discipline.
out_of_scope: Any second truth store or side-channel admission; any parity claim beyond what the bound owners prove.
implementation_actions: Map each QM state read/write to its canonical owner projection or admission path before any serving.
Rebind authority and harness surfaces; register served routes through the census epoch flow.
Prove fail-closed behavior for every absent owner.
positive_proof: The served surface renders live daemon truth with zero QM-local truth writes and typed refusals on every authority crossing.
adversarial_or_fault_proof: Reject QM-local truth writes, non-lease authority crossings, unregistered routes, plugin-resolved harnesses bypassing the registry, and success states rendered from absent owners.
compatibility_and_migration: The dormant tree remains the byte basis; rebinding is additive modules plus configuration, reversible to dormancy.

code_anchors.evidence_scope: the adapter-over-daemon-truth rebinding pattern the Hypervisor surface proved

remaining_nonclaims: Rebinding certifies only the bound owners' truth; it closes no stage and grants no wallet authority.
rollback_or_stop_rule: Stop if rebinding would create a second truth store, bypass CapabilityLease, or serve an unregistered route; roll back to the dormant tree.
source_provenance: Owner QM seed ruling 2026-08-02 (queued post-#133): executable rebind as act two, sequenced after the orchestration seam and participant/frontier closeout; filed by the implementer session as the first M5-branch batch.

canon_snapshot.snapshot_role: Provenance for the canon revision this record was authored against. Drift detection is owned by generated/canon-baseline.v1.json via tools/canon-impact.mjs.

aggregate_disposition.why: Owner ruling 2026-08-02: apps/ioi-ai/ SCAFFOLDING gates M5, and the dormant adoption is the scaffolding. Binding the rebind would extend the M5 exit from 'the seed is adopted' to 'the seed runs against canonical owners' — a scope increase the ruling did not make. This is a decision, not a hedge: the scaffold is gating, its execution is not. The earlier transitive concern (that binding the rebind would pull in the seam) is moot now that the seam and the event successor are bound children in their own right. AMENDED BY OWNER RULING 2026-08-02 (final): non-gating for M5 AND a named gating child of M6. The record is no longer merely excluded from one aggregate — it is bound into another, so the product intent (ioi-ai real, not parked) has a MECHANICAL home rather than an intention. m6-product-surface-and-typed-workspaces.aggregate_child_ids now names it, which means M6 cannot certify without ioi-ai executable against canonical owners, enforced by the same certify-stage machinery that governs every other child. Both dependencies are M5-gating children, so the moment M5 certifies this is immediately actionable as early M6 work.
